name: Gebrinius

attributes.attribute: is attested by ten inscriptions and a 2nd-century shrine at Bonn
was equated with Mars by Roman worshippers
may take his epithet from a word for goat
is shown with a lion-like head and a sheep-like body

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gebrinius, also called Mercurius Gebrinius, is a Continental Celtic deity known from ten inscriptions and a second-century shrine, all at Bonn in Germany. The Romans set him beside Mars in their warrior pantheon. Most of the record comes from the Ubii, a people of eastern Gaul, so the god may belong to a frontier zone where Celtic and Germanic worship met. The meaning of the epithet is not settled. One reading points to a horned god and compares Old Irish gabor and Welsh gafr, both meaning 'goat'. No firm parallel supports that view. Images show a creature with a lion-like head on a body closer to a fat sheep. The small corpus and the single cult place leave his character open.

okr.objective: Document Gebrinius as a poorly attested Continental deity of the Rhine frontier.
key_results: Fix the cult place at Bonn and the count of ten inscriptions.
Record the Roman equation with Mars and the title Mercurius Gebrinius.
State the disputed 'goat' etymology and the animal iconography.
